values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Kinder Morgan fact sheet says the Evangeline Pass Expansion Project supplies up to 1,100,000 dekatherms per day to Venture Global Plaquemines LNG's Gator Express Pipeline.

verifications.note: Fact sheet states the project's purpose is to supply Venture Global Plaquemines LNG's proposed Gator Express Pipeline.

records.researcher_notes: The sheet already had yes and Plaquemines LNG Terminal with no ref. The Kinder Morgan fact sheet names the project and states the Plaquemines LNG purpose, so the values stay and the ref is added.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Natural Gas Intelligence article from April 2018 says the FERC approval of the East-West Project adds laterals to serve Gulf Coast demand including LNG facilities. Two shippers, JERA Energy America and Shell Energy North America, are active in LNG markets.

verifications.note: Article says the East-West Project would serve Gulf Coast demand including LNG facilities; JERA and Shell are the shippers.

records.researcher_notes: The article is headlined as a project for LNG players but names no terminal, so the terminal is left blank. Deliveries go to a Motiva refinery point and a Coastal Bend point in Texas. The tie to LNG is through the shippers and the article's wording.

ledger.note: Searched Trinity River Supply Lateral with Sherman Extension and LNG. Trade press describes it as Barnett Shale takeaway capacity and none mention LNG.
Searched Equitrans Allegheny Valley Connector with LNG. Nothing ties this line to LNG export. The only LNG mentions found were general market comments.
Searched Ohio Valley Connector and LNG. A FERC notice for a later expansion mentions mid-continent and Gulf Coast markets, but no source ties this 2016 segment to an LNG terminal or LNG export.
Kept yes and Plaquemines LNG Terminal. A Kinder Morgan fact sheet states the project supplies Venture Global Plaquemines LNG's Gator Express Pipeline.
Searched Fayetteville Express Pipeline with LNG export and feedgas. Sources describe Fayetteville Shale takeaway to Trunkline and none name an LNG terminal or shipper.
The EIA notes say the East Louisiana Project adds a delivery point to Entergy Louisiana for power. No LNG tie was found in the EIA text or the existing refs.
A Natural Gas Intelligence article from April 2018 ties the East-West Project to Gulf Coast LNG facilities and names LNG-active shippers. No terminal is named.
